clue.text: Investigator probes organised crime using evidence

indicators.note: something that probes pushes its way into the middle of what it examines
the letters of crime are put into a new order

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A detective digs into organised crime with hard evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' makes EMRIC, and 'probes' sends the investigator into it. 'using evidence' looks like part of the crime story; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An empiric approach relies on observation and experiment, that is on evidence rather than theory.

clue.text: Top important figure

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: weighty means significant

explanation.surface: A leading personality is a big name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a person; it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty is a number, and a figure can mean a numeral.

clue.text: Writer brought back offended, eponymous hero

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: brought back means turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: sinned means transgressed, offended

explanation.surface: An author returns, upset by his own title character.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Pendennis is the title character of Thackeray's novel, so his name is the book's.

clue.text: Regret vocal jibe in stage whisper

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark

explanation.surface: An actor voices regret at a taunt, half under their breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras on stage repeat this word to simulate background chatter, a theatrical mutter.

clue.text: Petted dog, holding head

indicators.note: holding means the outer piece wraps around the inner one

parts.note: a dog can mean a contemptible man, a cad
noodle is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone stroked a dog while cradling its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Petted' looks like stroking an animal; it is the sense of kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, which is what petting means.

clue.text: Fire getting cold and greyer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ashier means paler, more grey, like ash

explanation.surface: A fire dies down, turning cold and grey with ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames; it is the verb meaning to sack, as officers once were.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them from service, a formal synonym of sacking.

clue.text: Animation about heraldic colour that's a palace favourite

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: CGI, computer-generated imagery, is used in animation
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A cartoon about a royal crest becomes a palace hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept this Welsh breed of dog at Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Trouble is after having favourable prognosis

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of is after are stirred up

explanation.surface: Trouble follows despite a good forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer reading of settled fine weather is a good forecast, a cheerful outlook.

clue.text: Northern home's inviting empty room

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: the loo is the smallest room, a euphemism for the toilet

explanation.surface: An Arctic dwelling with an inviting but bare room.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow house is a dwelling of the far north.

clue.text: I'm not sure about feminist opponent

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: er is a hesitant noise of uncertainty
sister is a term of solidarity among feminists

explanation.surface: Someone unsure about a feminist who opposes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who resists is one who stands against something, an adversary.

clue.text: Accelerate in front of athlete who moves arms

indicators.note: the first piece is placed before the second

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it hard
a runner is a track athlete

explanation.surface: An athlete speeds up, arms pumping as they run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves arms' suggests a sprinter's swinging arms; here arms are weapons being smuggled.
explanation.definitionFit: A smuggler of weapons transports arms illegally, so one who moves arms.

clue.text: Mass of rock crystal usually keeps hidden

indicators.note: the phrase crystal usually holds the letters within it, concealed across the gap between its words

explanation.surface: A rock formation usually conceals its crystals inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Talus is a sloping heap of rock fragments at a cliff foot, also called scree.

clue.text: Old name for soldiers sometimes showing character

parts.note: the reserve force was long called the Territorial Army
the TA were part-time soldiers, serving only sometimes

explanation.surface: A historical name for an army unit reveals something of its character.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TA was the familiar name for the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve, renamed the Army Reserve in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: A character can be a letter of an alphabet, and theta is the eighth Greek letter.

clue.text: Maybe broody old dignitary, a sour drunk

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of a sour are staggered about

explanation.surface: A moody, sour old bigwig has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A SOUR to AROUS. 'broody' looks like sulky; it is a hen sitting on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-laying animals are oviparous, and a broody hen is one example, hence the question-like 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Person who's decorated not one ring of gold

parts.note: no means not one, none
a bell is something that rings, a ring on the phone
aureate means golden, made of or like gold

explanation.surface: A decorated person is denied even a single gold ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nobel prizewinner is honoured with a medal and prize, so is someone decorated.

clue.text: Rating new filling dessert, able to take a lot in

definitions.text: able to take a lot in

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

indicators.note: filling means going inside

parts.note: a sorbet is an ice dessert

explanation.surface: A sailor stuffed with pudding can still eat more.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-officer sailor in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something porous that soaks up liquid readily can take a great deal in.

clue.text: Lack of balance provoked two lots of my tears

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters are mixed
two lots of means the word is taken twice

explanation.surface: An unbalanced outburst brings on floods of tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lopsided, the two sides not matching, is a want of balance.

clue.text: Son moved awkwardly, restrained

parts.note: waddled means walked with a clumsy rolling gait

explanation.surface: A boy shuffled clumsily, held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies wrapped tightly in cloth are bound so they cannot move freely.

clue.text: Player given hand aligns with person on the right film

parts.note: West is one of the four players dealt a hand at bridge
to side with someone is to align with them
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A card player picks a political side with a right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1961 musical film set among New York gangs, a famous title of the screen.

clue.text: Pay bonus money through post

indicators.note: through means passing within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
a tip is extra money for service

explanation.surface: Wages and a bonus arrive by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular allowance, such as a clergyman's salary.

clue.text: It's weird not having a partner round

parts.note: an odd sock or glove has lost its pair
a ball is round, a sphere

explanation.surface: It is strange to be left without a dance partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a turn of dancing; it is a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, used informally, it means eccentric or strange.

clue.text: Amount of volume by orchestra's principal music player

parts.note: a stere is a cubic metre, a unit of volume

indicators.note: principal means first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A loud orchestra is led by its principal musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'music player' looks like a musician; it is a hi-fi.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system with two speakers for playing records or discs.

clue.text: Weapon the German clutches doing wrong

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tightly, so the outer piece grips the inner one

parts.note: der is a German word for the
erring means straying, doing wrong

explanation.surface: A German grabs a weapon while committing a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol, a concealable handgun.

clue.text: Mostly, broadcaster and I spoke and spoke?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a radio is a broadcasting set

explanation.surface: A broadcaster and I mostly did the talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak; it is the rod of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoke of a wheel is a radius, so two spokes are its plural.

clue.text: Fish very quietly bound by rope

indicators.note: bound by means enclosed by, so one piece is surrounded

parts.note: a guy is a rope securing a tent
pp, pianissimo, is very quietly in music

explanation.surface: A fish is silently tied up with rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The guppy is a small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Counted the minutes to retreat or resign

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: timed means measured the minutes taken

explanation.surface: Someone watched the clock before choosing to withdraw or quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat or resign' looks like a pair of synonyms for the answer; only 'resign' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To demit is a formal word for to give up an office, step down.

clue.text: Juvenile article in Paris Match is a scoop

parts.note: a lad is a young boy
Paris Match is a French magazine, and an article in French is le

explanation.surface: A young reporter's story in a French magazine is an exclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a magazine story; it is the grammatical article, French le.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep spoon for serving soup, a kind of scoop.

clue.text: Sample by writer, one who's not very good

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer
a taster is a small sample

explanation.surface: A trial piece by an author proves rather poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of inferior verse, a poor versifier.

clue.text: Sort of material from one who's ineffectual and uninteresting

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person
dry means dull

explanation.surface: Some fabric comes from a weak, boring person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that dries smooth when hung wet, needing no ironing, is described this way.

clue.text: Cry to encourage friend in hot pants

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of hot are made a mess of

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A shout urges on a pal wearing hot pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) makes THO, which goes round the friend. 'pants' looks like clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox-hunter's shout on sighting the fox, urging hounds and riders on.
